history.dynasty: Modern (Shree Sanatan Dharam Sabha / local trust)
history.summary: Shri Krishna Mandir in Ludhiana's Model Town Extension (address: Krishna Mandir Rd, Model Town Extension, Ludhiana 141002) is one of the city's best-known Hindu temples. Built over roughly 500 sq yards, the temple holds more than 520 statues of Hindu deities, the most prominent being a 37-ft statue of Lord Hanuman. Janmashtami is celebrated on the open ground in front of the temple, and Dussehra and Maha Shivaratri are observed with glory. The temple runs a charitable hospital offering free treatment and medicines to the poor. No founding date or founder is given in available sources (verify).

town_description: Ludhiana is Punjab's largest city and India's largest industrial city, located about 100 km from Chandigarh on the Grand Trunk Road. A major hub of hosiery, bicycle and agricultural-implement manufacturing, it is also known for its temples, gurdwaras and cultural festivals such as Lohri, Basant Panchami and Baisakhi.
